newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Refugees say they fleeing army in Angolan enclave.
newsitem.headline: Refugees say they fleeing army in Angolan enclave.

text.p: Hundreds of villagers have fled their homes in the turbulent Angolan enclave of Cabinda because of attacks by the national army, refugees said on Wednesday.

"The soldiers came to our village and stole everything we had. They beat us and made us leave," said one man arriving in the town of Subantando with 15 other people from their village of Cinto Macanda along the border with Zaire.
"They accused us of being brothers of FLEC (Front for the Liberation of the Cabinda Enclave), but I am an old man with only one leg and what harm can I cause?"
FLEC and other rebel groups have been fighting for Cabinda's independence since the days of Portuguese rule in the 1960s.
The enclave of 300,000 people is separated from the rest of Angola by the Congo river and a small, peaceful strip of Zaire.
Refugees from Cinto and another village started arriving in Subantando on Monday after what villagers referred to as an Angolan army offensive that began in the area on Sunday.
Cinto mayor Domingos Cassimiro told Reuters that 250 refugees had arrived in Subantando, 30 km (18 miles) northeast of the regional capital Cabinda.
Catholic church sources in the capital say 12 villages have been depopulated by the latest of a string of sporadic army operations.
The province's vice-governor for defence, Colonel Henriques Futi, denied any wrongdoing by the army.

"This is not an offensive," he said. "I would call it manoeuvres instead. What these villagers have told you is not true. FLEC did this to them, they only blame the army because they know FLEC will kill them if they speak out. They know we will not harm them."
Villagers from a third village, Luavo, told a similar tale when they arrived on the outskirts of Cabinda city, blaming the army for attacks.
"There is nothing left in our village," said one teenager. "The army took everything and all the houses have been destroyed."
